subsystems.name: Reflector film
subsystems.role: a mirror large enough to intercept a useful share of the star's light, yet light enough to hover.
parts: substrate a few hundred nanometres thick

subsystems.name: Support structure
subsystems.role: holds the film flat and keeps it aimed, without adding so much mass that it falls into the star.

subsystems.name: Statite station-keeping
subsystems.role: keeps the mirror parked at the height where radiation pressure and gravity cancel, and steers the thrust.

subsystems.name: Damage management
subsystems.role: micrometeorites, thermal cycling and slow coating degradation would shred a thin film over long timescales.

subsystems.name: In-space industry
subsystems.role: everything the mirror is made of has to come from off-Earth material.

subsystems.name: Monitoring network
subsystems.role: tracks the sheet's shape and the orbits of every planet being carried along.

buildSteps.title: Choose a heading
buildSteps.detail: Any thrust vector changes the whole system's motion, so the destination and the star's remaining lifetime are fixed first.

buildSteps.title: Mine the feedstock
buildSteps.detail: Metal-rich asteroids or crustal rock are the plausible sources of iron, nickel and aluminium; the mass needed is on the order of a small moon.

buildSteps.title: Refine and roll the film
buildSteps.detail: Metal is smelted and drawn into foil or deposited as vapour onto a plastic-thin substrate, aiming for an areal density of a few grams per square metre.

buildSteps.title: Assemble in space
buildSteps.detail: Segments are joined into one large curved sheet at a fabrication site, with trusses and actuators attached.

buildSteps.title: Fly it to the hover point
buildSteps.detail: Because a flat reflector's radiation force and gravity both fall with distance in the same way, the sheet can hover at almost any height — so it is slowly spiralled outward to the chosen radius.

buildSteps.title: Trim the balance
buildSteps.detail: Mass is added or removed until light pressure exactly cancels the star's pull; the mirror is then no longer falling anywhere.

buildSteps.title: Start the thrust
buildSteps.detail: Tilting the sheet redirects the star's radiation into one hemisphere, and by conservation of momentum the star and its planets drift the other way at about 10⁻¹² m/s².

buildSteps.title: Operate for millions of years
buildSteps.detail: Robots patch holes and renew coatings while controllers watch that planetary orbits stay stable.

prerequisites.why: solar sails have flown since IKAROS in 2010, but nothing has been built at thousands-of-kilometres scale or a few grams per square metre.
the whole concept rests on a mirror that hangs motionless on starlight alone; this has never been demonstrated even in miniature.

prerequisites.tech: Off-Earth mining and manufacturing at gigatonne scale
prerequisites.why: the reflector has to be built from non-terrestrial material, which today is limited to gram-scale samples.
the sheet must survive micrometeorites and thermal cycling for geological time without crews.
we can model that a uniform acceleration far below the planets' binding force preserves their orbits, but not a real engine's irregularities.

pathway.milestone: small solar sails demonstrating radiation-pressure propulsion
pathway.unlocks: techniques for ultra-thin reflective films and attitude control.

pathway.milestone: orbital manufacturing from asteroid material at kilogram-to-tonne scale
pathway.unlocks: structures that can be built far larger than any rocket can launch.

pathway.milestone: a partial swarm of independent reflectors around the star
pathway.unlocks: stellar-scale power collection, plus a small incidental push on the star.

pathway.milestone: a coordinated single mirror parked at the balance point
pathway.unlocks: the Shkadov thruster proper — relocating an entire planetary system, first proposed by Leonid Shkadov in 1987.

pathway.milestone: active stellar engines that mine and expel stellar plasma
pathway.unlocks: faster travel, at a cost measured in the star's own lifetime.
